name: Robinson Hierarchy
desc: The hierarchy that proves a tiling can never repeat — Robinson's nested squares at every doubling scale, each square cross-braced to the four children inside it, the whole engraved lattice inflating forever through its own generations as a raking light drifts across the plate.

energy.doc: ink contrast + wash depth + line weight + chiaroscuro depth

scale.doc: motif size within its cell — 2 packs the squares edge to edge, 0.5 leaves them floating and airy (an endless zoom would swallow a plain size param, so scale drives proportion)

density.doc: how many generations deep the hierarchy is drawn at once

arms.doc: reach of the cross arms binding each square to its children

breathe.doc: how much the zoom breathes back and forth between inflating and coarsening

x.doc: hierarchy centre x as canvas fraction

y.doc: hierarchy centre y as canvas fraction

style.doc: aesthetic: sepia copperplate engraving / cyan schematic on prussian / leaded jewel glass in dark cames / luminous additive frames on black (non-representational) / raking-light brutalist concrete
